newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse rebounds after earnings reports.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse rebounds after earnings reports.

text.p: The Hungarian share market moved higher on Monday, rebounding from Friday's losses, as a new batch of corporate results were released this morning, traders said.
The BUX index finished at 5,586.69 points, up 66.29.
"The market corrected upwards Friday's falls," said Robert Cselovszki of WestLB Investment.
Leading issues, falling on Friday after they had released their 1996 earnings reports, rebounded and also many others, publishing their figures, joined the upward trend.
Chemicals TVK which plummeted 16 percent on Friday, regained more than half of this loss and closed at 2,390 forints, up 190, while Borsodchem rose 310 forints to end at 6,350.
Pharmaceuticals moved sharply higher, with Egis leading them by a 6.25 percent gain after CS First Boston said it maintained its 'buy' rating on Egis shares.

"The results and the company's partial forecast for 1997 reinforce our view on future earnings development, therefore we have chosen to leave our forecasts unchanged," Spencer Jakab, CSFB's Budapest-based analyst said in an update.

Oil company MOL shares bucked the bullish trend and slipped 25 forints to close at 3,170 as uncertainties about the timing and the pricing of MOL shares in the next phase of its privatisation remained.
"Many investors are on the sidelines ready to act and reinvest in MOL again but they can't decide when," Cselovszki said.

Hotel firm Danubius which firmed sharply on expectations of strong 1996 earnings, eased 50 forints to end at 5,950, after reporting its pre-tax profits rising to 2.67 billion forints from 2.06 billion in 1995.
Traders said it was difficult to predict short-term trend on the market.
"There was a major price increase and those who want to lock in profits, can still easily influence prices," Cselovszki said.
